words.definition: A greeting used when you meet someone or begin a conversation.
example_sentences: Hello, how are you?
Hello, is this seat next to you free?

words.definition: An informal greeting used when you meet or speak to someone.
example_sentences: Hi, it's good to see you again after the holidays.
Hi, I'm Maya, and I'll be showing you around the office.

words.definition: A very informal greeting, often used with someone you know.
example_sentences: Hey, come in and put your bag on the chair.
Hey, I saved you a seat near the window.

words.definition: An expression used when you leave someone or end a conversation.
example_sentences: Goodbye, see you tomorrow.
Goodbye, and thank you for having us over for dinner.

words.definition: An informal way to say goodbye when you leave or end a conversation.
example_sentences: Bye, everyone; I need to catch my bus.
Bye, Dad; I'll call you when the train arrives.

words.definition: A friendly way to say goodbye when you expect to meet someone again.
example_sentences: See you later; we can finish our conversation after class.
See you later; I'll meet you outside the cinema at six.

words.definition: A polite greeting used during the morning.
example_sentences: Good morning, everyone; I hope you slept well.
Good morning, Ms. Lee; your first appointment is here.

words.definition: A polite greeting used after noon and before the evening.
example_sentences: Good afternoon, please come in and take a seat.
Good afternoon, I'd like to check in for my appointment.

words.definition: A polite greeting used when you meet someone in the evening.
example_sentences: Good evening, and welcome to our school concert.
Good evening, do you have a table for two?

words.definition: An expression used when saying goodbye at night or going to bed.
example_sentences: Good night, sleep well, and I'll see you at breakfast.
Good night, everyone; I'm going upstairs to bed.

words.definition: An expression that shows you are pleased someone has arrived or joined you.
example_sentences: Welcome home; we've made your favorite meal.
Welcome to our team; we're glad you're here.

words.definition: A friendly goodbye that expresses a wish for someone to stay safe and well.
example_sentences: Take care, and I'll see you when you're back from your trip.
Take care, and let me know when you get home safely.

words.definition: A word added to a request to make it more polite.
example_sentences: Please sit down.
Could you please turn the music down while I work?

words.definition: An expression used to show appreciation for something someone has done.
example_sentences: Thank you for your help.
Thank you for waiting while I found my ticket.

words.definition: An informal expression of gratitude for help, a gift, or another kind action.
example_sentences: Thanks a lot for helping me carry those heavy bags.
Thanks for lending me your umbrella in the rain.

words.definition: A polite reply when someone thanks you.
example_sentences: You're welcome; it was no trouble to give you a ride.
You're welcome; I'm glad the directions helped.

words.definition: Feeling regret about a mistake or something that has caused trouble; used when apologizing.
example_sentences: I'm sorry I'm late; my bus broke down on the way here.
I'm sorry I spilled juice on your notebook.

words.definition: A polite expression used to get attention, interrupt, or ask someone to let you pass.
example_sentences: Excuse me, can I get by?
Excuse me, where can I buy a bus ticket?

words.definition: A polite request for someone to repeat something you did not hear or understand.
example_sentences: Pardon? Could you say that again?
Pardon? I couldn't hear the address over the traffic.

words.definition: An informal way to say that something is acceptable or that you are happy to help.
example_sentences: No problem, I can wait.
No problem; you can return the book next week.

words.definition: An expression used to agree willingly or show that something is certainly allowed or true.
example_sentences: Of course, I'll help you.
Of course you can borrow my charger; it's on the desk.

words.definition: A conventional expression said to someone just after they sneeze.
example_sentences: Bless you! Are you getting a cold?
Bless you! There's a box of tissues beside you.

words.definition: An expression used to celebrate someone's achievement or happy news.
example_sentences: Congratulations on your new job!
Congratulations on finishing your first marathon!

words.definition: An informal expression used when raising a drink in celebration; also used to mean thank you, especially in British English.
example_sentences: Cheers, everyone; let's celebrate our first year together!
Cheers for the ride; you saved me a long walk in the rain.

words.definition: A polite expression used when you are introduced to someone for the first time.
example_sentences: It's nice to meet you; I'm Ana from the apartment upstairs.
Nice to meet you, Luis; I've heard a lot about your work.

words.definition: An expression used to introduce yourself by stating your name.
example_sentences: My name is Ana.
My name is Daniel, and I have a reservation for tonight.

words.definition: An expression used to introduce or identify a person or thing.
example_sentences: This is my friend, Sam.
This is Priya, who will be teaching our class this term.

words.definition: A person you know well and like.
example_sentences: She's a close friend who always listens when I need advice.
I called a friend to ask for help moving my sofa.

words.definition: A person who lives near you.
example_sentences: Our neighbor waved hello.
Our neighbor watered the plants while we were away.

words.definition: A person in the same class as you.
example_sentences: My classmate helped me study.
I borrowed a pencil from the classmate sitting beside me.

words.definition: A person you work with.
example_sentences: A colleague called me.
My colleague covered my shift when I was sick.

words.definition: A person you do not know.
example_sentences: Don't talk to strangers.
A stranger at the station helped me lift my suitcase.

words.definition: To make two people known to each other.
example_sentences: Let me introduce you to my boss.
I'd like to introduce our new teacher to the class.

words.definition: A greeting made by joining and shaking hands.
example_sentences: They exchanged a handshake.
The interview ended with a firm handshake and a smile.

words.definition: A question used to ask about someone's health, feelings, or general well-being.
example_sentences: How are you today, and did you manage to get some rest?
How are you feeling after your long journey?

words.definition: A friendly question about how someone feels or how things are going for them.
example_sentences: How are you doing since you started your new job?
How are you doing now that you've settled into your new home?

words.definition: Feeling well or in a satisfactory condition, without a particular problem.
example_sentences: I'm fine, thanks.
My ankle feels fine now, so I can walk to the shop.

words.definition: Very good, enjoyable, or pleasing.
example_sentences: I feel great today.
Your soup tastes great; could I have the recipe?

words.definition: Acceptable or reasonably well, even if not especially good.
example_sentences: I'm okay, thanks for asking.
The room is small, but it's okay for a one-night stay.

words.definition: Fairly good or satisfactory; often used as a modest positive reply.
example_sentences: Not bad, and you?
The sandwich was not bad, though it needed a little more salt.

words.definition: Neither particularly good nor particularly bad.
example_sentences: I feel so-so today.
The service was excellent, but the food was only so-so.

words.definition: An expression used to ask someone the same question they just asked you.
example_sentences: I'm well, and you?
I live near the park, and you?

words.definition: An informal question asking what is happening, what is new, or what is wrong.
example_sentences: What's up, Alex? I haven't seen you since the weekend.
What's up, Sam? You look worried about something.

words.definition: The number 0, used to show that there is none of something.
example_sentences: The score is zero.
Our team finished the match with zero points.

words.definition: The number 1, used for a single person or thing.
example_sentences: I have one brother.
We only need one more chair for everyone to sit down.

words.definition: The number 2, which is one more than one.
example_sentences: I packed two books to read on the train.
I'd like two tickets for the afternoon show, please.

words.definition: The number 3, which is one more than two.
example_sentences: We need three chairs for the visitors in the waiting room.
The recipe needs three eggs and a cup of milk.

words.definition: The number 4, which is one more than three.
example_sentences: This car has four doors, so it's easy for everyone to get in.
Four people can sit comfortably at this table.

words.definition: The number 5, which is one more than four.
example_sentences: I bought five apples to make a pie.
The bus leaves in five minutes, so we should hurry.

words.definition: The number 10, equal to two groups of five.
example_sentences: This notebook costs ten dollars at the shop near my school.
I paid ten dollars for this secondhand jacket.

words.definition: The number 20, equal to two groups of ten.
example_sentences: Twenty students signed up for the cooking class.
There are twenty questions on the history test.

words.definition: The number 100, equal to ten groups of ten.
example_sentences: A hundred people came.
The library received a hundred new books this month.

words.definition: The number 1,000, equal to ten groups of one hundred.
example_sentences: This old building has stood here for nearly a thousand years.
More than a thousand people watched the concert in the park.

words.definition: Coming before all others in an order or sequence.
example_sentences: The first train leaves at six.
Read the first paragraph before you answer the questions.

words.definition: Coming immediately after the first in an order or sequence.
example_sentences: The bathroom is behind the second door on the left.
We missed the first bus, but caught the second one.

words.definition: One of two equal parts.
example_sentences: Half the pie is gone.
We saved half of the cake for our guests tomorrow.

words.definition: The point in a day measured in hours and minutes, usually shown by a clock.
example_sentences: What time is it?
Please check the time so we don't miss our train.

words.definition: A unit of time equal to sixty minutes.
example_sentences: Wait one hour.
The museum is an hour away by bus.

words.definition: A unit of time equal to sixty seconds.
example_sentences: Wait a minute.
The doors will open in one minute, so have your ticket ready.

words.definition: An expression placed after a number to state an exact hour, without minutes.
example_sentences: It's three o'clock.
Our table is booked for seven o'clock this evening.

words.definition: The part of the day from midnight until noon, especially the hours after waking.
example_sentences: I like to take a short walk in the morning before work.
I drink a glass of water every morning before breakfast.

words.definition: The part of the day between noon and evening.
example_sentences: We have a meeting this afternoon to discuss the new schedule.
Let's visit the museum this afternoon after lunch.

words.definition: The part of the day between late afternoon and the time people usually go to bed.
example_sentences: I'm going to call my parents this evening after dinner.
We spent the evening cooking and talking with friends.

words.definition: The period of darkness between the end of one day and the beginning of the next.
example_sentences: I close the curtains at night so the streetlights don't keep me awake.
The streets are much quieter at night.

words.definition: At the present time or at this particular moment.
example_sentences: Do it now.
The oven is hot now, so we can put the bread in.

words.definition: At a time after the present or after another time already mentioned.
example_sentences: We can watch the film later tonight when everyone gets home.
I'll answer your message later, after my meeting.

words.definition: Happening or arriving before the usual or expected time.
example_sentences: I booked an early train to avoid the busiest part of the morning.
We took an early flight so we could arrive before lunch.

words.definition: Happening or arriving after the expected or usual time.
example_sentences: Sorry I'm late.
The delivery was late because the road was closed.

words.definition: The day that is happening now.
example_sentences: We're visiting our cousins today because everyone has the day off.
We need to finish packing today because we leave in the morning.

words.definition: The day immediately after today.
example_sentences: See you tomorrow.
The shop is closed today but will open again tomorrow.

words.definition: The day immediately before today.
example_sentences: It was cold yesterday, so we wore our winter coats.
I left my umbrella at the restaurant yesterday.

words.definition: The day of the week after Sunday and before Tuesday.
example_sentences: I work on Monday.
Our new course begins on Monday at nine in the morning.

words.definition: The day of the week after Thursday and before Saturday.
example_sentences: We're going to see a play on Friday night.
We're having dinner with friends on Friday after work.

words.definition: The day of the week after Saturday and before Monday.
example_sentences: I rest on Sunday.
The market opens later on Sunday than on Saturday.

words.definition: A period of seven consecutive days.
example_sentences: I'm working from home this week while the office is being repaired.
I'm staying with my sister for a week while my flat is being painted.

words.definition: One of the twelve named periods in a calendar year, lasting from twenty-eight to thirty-one days.
example_sentences: My sister is moving into her new apartment next month.
I put a little money into my savings account every month.

words.definition: A period of twelve months, normally containing 365 days or 366 in a leap year.
example_sentences: I hope to finish my course next year.
She spent a year studying in another country.

words.definition: The first month of the calendar year, between December and February.
example_sentences: My little brother was born in January, during a snowstorm.
The new bus timetable takes effect in January.

words.definition: The sixth month of the calendar year, between May and July.
example_sentences: School ends in June.
Our cousins are coming to visit us in June.

words.definition: The twelfth month of the calendar year, between November and January.
example_sentences: We often get snow in December where I live.
The shop stays open late during December.

words.definition: A period of twenty-four hours, from one midnight to the next.
example_sentences: It was a long day, so we went straight to bed after dinner.
We spent a whole day exploring the old town.

words.definition: The part of the week when many people have time off work or school, usually Saturday and Sunday.
example_sentences: We're visiting our grandparents this weekend.
I'm planning to fix my bicycle this weekend.

words.definition: A period of the year with characteristic weather, such as spring, summer, autumn, or winter.
example_sentences: Summer is my favorite season.
The trees change color during the autumn season.
words.simple_gloss: one of four parts of the year

words.definition: Every time or on all occasions.
example_sentences: She always smiles.
He always checks that the door is locked before leaving.

words.definition: Many times or on many occasions, but not necessarily every time.
example_sentences: I often walk to work.
This café is often full at lunchtime.

words.definition: On some occasions, but not often or always.
example_sentences: I sometimes cook at home.
Sometimes we take the train instead of driving.

words.definition: Not at any time or on any occasion.
example_sentences: I never smoke.
She has never visited the coast, but she would like to go.

words.definition: After a short time; not far into the future.
example_sentences: I'll see you soon when I come over for dinner.
The rain should stop soon, and then we can walk home.

words.definition: Feeling pleased, cheerful, or satisfied about something.
example_sentences: She looks happy today.
I was happy to hear that my sister had arrived safely.

words.definition: Feeling unhappy, often because of a loss or an unpleasant experience.
example_sentences: He felt sad after the news.
We felt sad when our neighbors moved to another city.

words.definition: Feeling strong displeasure because something seems wrong, unfair, or upsetting.
example_sentences: Don't be angry with me.
She was angry because someone had damaged her bicycle.

words.definition: Needing rest or sleep because your energy has been used up.
example_sentences: I'm too tired to go out.
After working all night, he was too tired to drive home.

words.definition: Feeling uneasy because you think something bad or difficult may happen.
example_sentences: She's worried about the test.
I'm worried that we won't reach the airport in time.

words.definition: Feeling very happy and interested, especially about something you expect to happen.
example_sentences: The kids are excited about the trip.
She's excited to start her first job next week.

words.definition: Feeling slightly angry or irritated by something unpleasant or inconvenient.
example_sentences: I'm annoyed that the bus is late.
He looked annoyed when his phone rang during the film.

words.definition: Unable to understand something clearly or decide what it means.
example_sentences: I'm confused by these instructions.
The two maps show different routes, and now I'm confused.

words.definition: Feeling afraid because you think there may be danger or harm.
example_sentences: I'm scared of the dark.
Don't be scared — I'm here.

words.definition: Unhappy because you feel alone or lack the company you want.
example_sentences: He felt lonely in the new city.
Call me if you get lonely.

words.definition: Feeling pleased about your own achievement or about someone you care about.
example_sentences: I'm proud of you.
She was proud of her work.

words.definition: Feeling uninterested because something is dull or there is nothing engaging to do.
example_sentences: I'm bored at home.
He became bored during the long class.

words.definition: Feeling worried or tense about something that may happen.
example_sentences: She's nervous about the interview.
I get nervous before I speak.

words.definition: Relaxed and in control of your feelings, without strong worry or anger.
example_sentences: Stay calm and breathe.
His voice was calm.

words.definition: Feeling that something is unexpected or different from what you thought would happen.
example_sentences: I was surprised to see you.
She looked surprised.

words.definition: Feeling uncomfortable or self-conscious because of an awkward situation or mistake.
example_sentences: I felt embarrassed when I forgot her name.
Don't be embarrassed to ask.

words.definition: Unhappy because something was not as good as you hoped or expected.
example_sentences: We were disappointed by the news.
I'm disappointed you didn't come.
words.simple_gloss: sad it wasn't what you hoped

words.definition: Feeling thankful for help, kindness, or something good that has happened.
example_sentences: I'm grateful for your help.
She was grateful they waited.

words.definition: Unhappy, worried, or disturbed by something that has happened.
example_sentences: He's upset about the mistake.
Don't get upset — we can fix it.

words.definition: Unhappy because someone else has something you want or receives attention you want.
example_sentences: Don't be jealous of her success.
He felt jealous of his brother.

words.definition: To receive something or obtain it by buying, finding, or asking for it.
example_sentences: Did you get my message?
You can get fresh bread at the bakery across the street.

words.definition: To pass something to someone or provide it for them.
example_sentences: Give her the keys.
Could you give this note to the teacher when you see her?

words.definition: To carry or move someone or something from one place to another.
example_sentences: Take an umbrella.
Please take these empty plates to the kitchen.

words.definition: To take someone or something with you toward the person or place being discussed.
example_sentences: Bring your laptop to class.
Can you bring some water when you come upstairs?

words.definition: To go away from a place or from someone.
example_sentences: I leave at eight.
We should leave the house before the traffic gets heavy.

words.definition: To remain in a place instead of leaving it.
example_sentences: Stay here until I come back.
Let's stay indoors until the storm passes.

words.definition: To continue to have something rather than giving it away or losing it.
example_sentences: You can keep the change.
Keep your receipt in case you need to return the shoes.

words.definition: To move something into a particular place or position.
example_sentences: Put the bag on the chair.
Please put the milk back in the fridge after breakfast.

words.definition: To choose one thing or person from several possibilities.
example_sentences: Pick a color.
You can pick any book from the shelf to read tonight.

words.definition: To take hold of something quickly or suddenly.
example_sentences: Grab your coat.
I had to grab the railing when the bus stopped suddenly.

words.definition: To keep something in your hand or maintain it in a particular position.
example_sentences: Hold my bag, please.
Could you hold the door open while I carry these boxes through?

words.definition: Stay until something happens.
example_sentences: Wait for me outside.
Can you wait a minute?

words.definition: Discover or locate something.
example_sentences: I can't find my keys.
Did you find a seat?

words.definition: Stop having something.
example_sentences: Don't lose the ticket.
I always lose my phone.

words.definition: Move something so it is not closed.
example_sentences: Open the window, please.
She opened the door.

words.definition: Move something so it is shut.
example_sentences: Close the door behind you.
He closed his laptop.

words.definition: To begin an activity or make something begin to happen.
example_sentences: Let's start the meeting.
The movie starts at eight.

words.definition: End an action or motion.
example_sentences: Stop at the light.
Can you stop talking for a second?

words.definition: To make a task or situation easier for someone by doing something useful.
example_sentences: Can you help me with this?
She helped him move.

words.definition: To do something with an object, tool, or resource for a particular purpose.
example_sentences: Use a pen, not a pencil.
I used your charger.

words.definition: To speak or write a question in order to get information or help.
example_sentences: Ask her what time it starts.
You can ask the driver which stop is nearest to the museum.

words.definition: To give someone information by speaking or writing to them.
example_sentences: Tell me what happened.
Please tell the receptionist that I've arrived for my appointment.

words.definition: To express something in spoken words.
example_sentences: What did she say?
She wanted to say something, but the meeting had already ended.

words.definition: To speak with someone in order to share information, ideas, or feelings.
example_sentences: We need to talk.
We like to talk about our day while we make dinner.

words.definition: To make something clear by describing it or giving reasons for it.
example_sentences: Can you explain this again?
The guide will explain how the old clock works.

words.definition: To refer to someone or something briefly without discussing it in detail.
example_sentences: She didn't mention the price.
Did he mention that the shop closes early on Fridays?

words.definition: To express or represent an idea; also, to intend something.
example_sentences: What does this word mean?
I didn't mean to interrupt.

words.definition: Pay attention to sound.
example_sentences: Listen to this song.
She listened carefully.

words.definition: To become aware of a sound through your ears, whether or not you are listening deliberately.
example_sentences: Did you hear that loud crash outside?
I can't hear you.

words.definition: To produce words with your voice or communicate with someone by talking.
example_sentences: Can you speak slower?
He spoke to the manager.

words.definition: To respond to a question, message, or call.
example_sentences: Please answer the phone.
She answered my email.

words.definition: Respond to a message or comment.
example_sentences: I'll reply later today.
He didn't reply.

words.definition: Put words on paper or a screen.
example_sentences: Write your name here.
She wrote a short note.

words.definition: Look at words and understand them.
example_sentences: I read the message twice.
Read this paragraph out loud so everyone can hear it.

words.definition: Phone someone or say their name.
example_sentences: I'll call you tonight.
Call me when you arrive.

words.definition: Talk about something with someone.
example_sentences: Let's discuss the plan.
We discussed it after class.

words.definition: To have the same opinion as someone or accept a shared decision.
example_sentences: I agree with you.
We both agree that the smaller apartment is the better choice.

words.definition: To have an opinion that is different from someone else's.
example_sentences: I disagree, but I hear you.
It's possible to disagree with someone and still respect their opinion.

words.definition: To offer an idea or possible course of action for someone to consider.
example_sentences: I suggest we leave early.
Could you suggest a quiet place where we can have lunch?

words.definition: To say firmly that you will do something or that something will happen.
example_sentences: I promise I'll call.
Don't promise to help if you know you won't have time.

words.definition: To have information about something or be familiar with it.
example_sentences: I know the answer.
Do you know which platform our train leaves from?

words.definition: To use your mind to consider something or form an idea.
example_sentences: Let me think about it.
I need a few minutes to think before I make a decision.

words.definition: To accept that something is true or that someone is telling the truth.
example_sentences: I believe you.
I didn't believe the story until I saw the photographs.

words.definition: To bring something back into your mind or continue to keep it in your memory.
example_sentences: Do you remember her name?
I always remember my grandmother's advice when I feel nervous.

words.definition: To fail to remember something or fail to do something because you did not remember it.
example_sentences: Don't forget your keys.
I was so busy that I forgot to eat lunch.

words.definition: To know the meaning of something or how it works.
example_sentences: I understand the question.
Do you understand now?

words.definition: To gain knowledge or a skill through study, experience, or practice.
example_sentences: I want to learn Spanish.
She learned it quickly.

words.definition: To think about something because you want to know or understand it.
example_sentences: I wonder where they went.
She wondered if he was okay.

words.definition: To form an idea or picture in your mind of something that is not present.
example_sentences: Imagine you are on a beach.
I can't imagine living there.

words.definition: To want something to happen while recognizing that it may not happen.
example_sentences: I hope you feel better.
We hope it doesn't rain.

words.definition: To feel uncertain that something is true, likely, or reliable.
example_sentences: I doubt that's true.
She doubted the story.

words.definition: To give your attention to one thing rather than letting it move to other things.
example_sentences: Focus on the question.
He couldn't focus in class.

words.definition: To decide in advance what you will do and how you will do it.
example_sentences: Let's plan the weekend.
She planned every step.

words.definition: To select the person or thing you want from the available options.
example_sentences: Choose a seat.
You can choose the movie.

words.definition: To become aware of something or begin to understand it clearly.
example_sentences: I realize I was wrong.
I didn't realize the café was closed until I reached the door.

words.definition: To become aware of something by seeing, hearing, or paying attention to it.
example_sentences: Did you notice the sign?
She was the first person to notice the missing picture.

words.definition: To give an answer or opinion without having enough information to be certain.
example_sentences: Guess who called.
I don't know the answer, but I'll try to guess.

words.definition: To make a choice after considering the possibilities.
example_sentences: We need to decide now.
We haven't decided where to spend the holidays yet.

words.definition: Of a high standard, useful, or pleasant.
example_sentences: That's a good idea.
This is a good place to sit and read quietly.

words.definition: Of poor quality or unpleasant; also, no longer fresh or safe to eat.
example_sentences: That was a bad movie.
The milk smells bad, so we should throw it away.

words.definition: Possible to do or understand without much effort or difficulty.
example_sentences: This homework is easy.
The instructions are easy to follow, even for a beginner.

words.definition: Difficult to do, understand, or achieve.
example_sentences: The test was hard.
It was hard to hear the speaker over the noise.

words.definition: Having enough value or influence that it deserves attention or care.
example_sentences: This is an important meeting.
It's important to save your work before turning off the computer.

words.definition: Not the same as another person or thing.
example_sentences: We have different opinions.
These two keys look alike, but they open different doors.

words.definition: Alike in some ways, but not exactly the same.
example_sentences: Our names are similar.
The twins have similar voices, so I sometimes confuse them on the phone.

words.definition: Pleasant, attractive, or kind toward other people.
example_sentences: That's a nice jacket.
She was nice to me.

words.definition: Strange or unusual in a way that attracts attention.
example_sentences: That's a weird noise.
I heard a weird clicking sound coming from the fridge.

words.definition: Sincere rather than joking; also, important enough to need careful attention.
example_sentences: I'm being serious.
This is a serious problem, and we need to deal with it today.

words.definition: Usual, typical, or expected in a particular situation.
example_sentences: That's a normal question.
It's normal to feel nervous before your first day at work.

words.definition: Able to happen or be done.
example_sentences: Is it possible to finish today?
Would it be possible to move our appointment to Friday?

words.definition: Free to help or meet; also, ready to be used or obtained.
example_sentences: Are you available at 3?
There are no rooms available at the hotel this weekend.

words.definition: Prepared or in a suitable condition for something to happen.

example_sentences: As far as I know, the library is still open on Saturdays.
The meeting is in Room 4, as far as I know, but I'll check the email.

words.definition: An expression used to make clear that you are giving your own view rather than stating a fact.
example_sentences: In my opinion, the shorter route is safer for cyclists.
The film's ending was too sudden, in my opinion, although I enjoyed the rest.

words.definition: An expression used to introduce a specific case that helps explain a general point.
example_sentences: You can save energy in several ways; for example, turn off lights in empty rooms.
Some birds cannot fly; penguins, for example, move well through water instead.

words.definition: An expression used to introduce a contrasting fact or another way of considering a situation.
example_sentences: The apartment is small; on the other hand, it's close to my office.
Driving would be faster, but on the other hand, the train would let us relax.

words.definition: An expression used to introduce what you really think or feel, especially if it may be unexpected.
example_sentences: To be honest, I found the instructions difficult to follow.
I said I was busy, but to be honest, I just needed a quiet evening at home.

words.definition: An expression meaning that your answer or decision changes according to the circumstances.
example_sentences: It depends on the weather; if it rains, we'll have lunch indoors.
Can I finish the repair today? It depends on whether the replacement part arrives.

words.definition: An expression used to say that an explanation or idea is reasonable and understandable.
example_sentences: That makes sense; leaving earlier should help us avoid the traffic.
Now you've explained why the price changed, that makes sense to me.

words.definition: An expression used to say that you do not know something confidently or have not made a decision.
example_sentences: I'm not sure which bus goes to the museum, so let's ask the driver.
I'm not sure I can attend on Friday; I need to check my work schedule.

words.definition: A polite request for someone to say something again because you did not hear or understand it.
example_sentences: Could you repeat that more slowly? I missed the last part of the address.
Could you repeat that, please? The announcement was too loud for me to hear you.

words.definition: To make a light, machine, or device start working by using its control.
example_sentences: Please turn on the kitchen light so I can read the recipe.
I turn on the radio in the morning to hear the traffic report.

words.definition: To make a light, machine, or device stop working by using its control.
example_sentences: Remember to turn off the oven when the bread is ready.
Can you turn off the television while we discuss the plans?

words.definition: To try to find someone or something.
example_sentences: I need to look for my keys before we can leave.
We're going to look for a quieter place to have lunch.

words.definition: To discover a fact or obtain information that you did not know before.
example_sentences: We need to find out what time the last train leaves.
You can find out whether the book is available by checking the library website.

words.definition: To stop trying to do something because it seems too difficult or is no longer worth the effort.
example_sentences: Don't give up on the puzzle yet; you've nearly finished it.
After several unsuccessful attempts, we decided to give up and ask for help.

words.definition: To delay an activity or move it to a later time.
example_sentences: Let's not put off fixing the leak until it gets worse.
She decided to put off her trip until her exams were over.

words.definition: To use all of a supply so that none remains.
example_sentences: We might run out of milk before breakfast, so I'll buy some now.
The printer will stop if we run out of paper during the job.

words.definition: To have a friendly or comfortable relationship with someone.
example_sentences: I get along with my new neighbors, and we often share gardening tips.
It's easier to get along with a roommate when you discuss chores early.

words.definition: To take care of someone or something and make sure they have what they need.
example_sentences: Could you look after my plants while I'm on holiday?
She helps look after her younger brother when their parents work late.

words.definition: To solve a problem or reach an answer by thinking, planning, or calculating.
example_sentences: We need to work out how much paint the room will need.
Let's work out a schedule that gives everyone a fair share of the weekend shifts.

words.definition: To do or say something that helps people feel more comfortable when they first meet.
example_sentences: The teacher used a short guessing game to break the ice on the first day.
I asked about her dog to break the ice before our interview.

words.definition: Something that is very easy to do; an informal expression.
example_sentences: After practicing all week, the final exercise was a piece of cake.
Finding the station was a piece of cake because there were signs on every corner.

words.definition: Feeling slightly ill or less well than usual.
example_sentences: I'm feeling under the weather, so I'll stay home and rest this evening.
She sounded under the weather on the phone and said she had a sore throat.

words.definition: Sharing the same understanding, information, or expectations about something.
example_sentences: Before we book anything, let's make sure we're on the same page about the budget.
The team wasn't on the same page, so we wrote down the plan together.

words.definition: Very rarely or almost never.
example_sentences: We only eat at that expensive restaurant once in a blue moon.
My old school friend lives abroad, so I see her once in a blue moon.

words.definition: After a long period of time, when the overall result becomes clear.
example_sentences: The stronger shoes cost more now, but they should save me money in the long run.
Learning to cook takes practice, but it makes everyday life easier in the long run.

words.definition: To learn how to do or use something through practice.
example_sentences: It took me a few tries to get the hang of the new coffee machine.
You'll get the hang of riding a bike if you keep practicing in a quiet place.

words.definition: To watch someone or something carefully for a short time or check on it regularly.
example_sentences: Could you keep an eye on my bag while I buy the tickets?
Please keep an eye on the soup so it doesn't boil over.

words.content: the ball is in your court
words.definition: It is now your responsibility or opportunity to decide what happens next.
example_sentences: I've sent you the proposal, so the ball is in your court now.
The landlord has offered a lower rent; the ball is in your court if you still want the apartment.

words.definition: To lose an opportunity because you act too late.
example_sentences: Book soon if you want the discounted tickets; you don't want to miss the boat.
I kept delaying my application and missed the boat when the course filled up.

words.definition: A saying that encourages regular practice as a way to improve a skill.
example_sentences: My piano teacher reminds me that practice makes perfect when a new piece feels difficult.
Practice makes perfect, so we rehearse the presentation a little every day.

words.definition: A saying that it is better to do something after the expected time than not to do it at all.
example_sentences: I finally wrote the thank-you note a month after the party; better late than never.
He started learning to swim at sixty, saying that it was better late than never.

words.definition: A saying that what people do shows their intentions more clearly than what they say.
example_sentences: She promised to help, but actions speak louder than words, so I waited to see whether she arrived.
He quietly repaired the fence instead of making another promise; actions speak louder than words.

words.content: two heads are better than one
words.definition: A saying that two people working together may solve a problem more effectively than one person alone.
example_sentences: Let's check the timetable together; two heads are better than one.
I asked my colleague to review the design because two heads are better than one.

words.content: don't count your chickens before they hatch
words.definition: A warning not to rely on a good result before it is certain.
example_sentences: Don't count your chickens before they hatch; wait for the job offer before planning how to spend the salary.
She told me not to count my chickens before they hatch when I assumed our team would win the final.

words.definition: Advice to consider the possible risks and consequences before taking action.
example_sentences: Look before you leap: read the rental agreement before you sign it.
My brother reminded me to look before I leap when I wanted to buy the first car I saw.

words.content: where there's a will, there's a way
words.definition: A saying that determination can help a person find a way through a difficult problem.
example_sentences: She built a ramp from spare wood to solve the access problem, showing that where there's a will, there's a way.
“Where there's a will, there's a way,” he said as he looked for an evening course that fit around his job.

words.content: all that glitters is not gold
words.definition: A warning that something attractive or impressive may not be as valuable or good as it appears.
example_sentences: The hotel photographs looked wonderful, but the rooms were dirty; all that glitters is not gold.
All that glitters is not gold, so compare the actual costs before choosing the most impressive offer.

words.content: a journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step
words.definition: A saying that a large or difficult task starts with one small action.
example_sentences: A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step, so I began my study plan with ten minutes of reading.
When the project felt overwhelming, we remembered that a journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.

words.content: every cloud has a silver lining
words.definition: A saying that an unpleasant situation may still have a positive side or lead to something good.
example_sentences: Missing the train gave us time to explore a lovely village, so perhaps every cloud has a silver lining.
Every cloud has a silver lining: losing that job led her to a career she enjoyed much more.
